I will do it mostly the way I did before, then I will push a little where I think yield can come safer. I have only 9.2 mu, so every bag I buy matters, but if I cut fertilizer too hard and lose grain, that hurts worse. Around Quzhou, with well water, people who get decent harvests do not farm light. For winter wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough base fertilizer in, water it a few times, and keep an eye on aphids and disease. For summer maize after wheat, I will go with hybrid seed, sow quickly after harvest, keep the field clean, give enough nitrogen, and water when the crop is setting ears if the rain is short. I do what I have seen work on nearby fields: wheat needs steady management and maize needs fast sowing after wheat plus enough fertilizer. I will keep tillage simple with rotary tillage because it is cheaper and faster for my size, and family labor is not always fully available.
